summary: Build practical digital revenue administration skills in compliance analytics, e-services, and process redesign. Enquire about an applied cohort.
lede: Digital Revenue Administration and Data-Driven Compliance equips revenue agencies and local governments to identify leakage, taxpayer friction, processing delays, and weak follow-up across the collection chain. You will learn to connect registration, filing, payment, arrears, dispute handling, and reporting through a TADAT-informed diagnostic and evidence-led operating approach. You will create practical outputs including process maps, compliance risk registers, service blueprints, control checklists, and performance dashboards. Through BPMN 2.0 mapping, risk segmentation, payment-channel design, service prioritisation, Power BI dashboard construction, and data-quality review, you will practise designing proportionate digital services and prioritising compliance interventions.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage public revenue collection, taxpayer services, compliance operations, finance reform, and government digital delivery. It suits intermediate and advanced practitioners who can bring a live or representative revenue process to the exercises.
audience: Ministry of Finance Revenue Policy Specialist
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to tax administration, public finance, municipal or national revenue operations, government digital services, audit, or revenue policy. No coding or programming is required. Bring a representative revenue process, anonymised performance data, or a current reform challenge if available. Advanced analytics, API architecture, and automation are addressed at conceptual or operational application level rather than production engineering level.
